title: Ash's Moonlit Question
markdown:
The Northwind Heights sparkled softly in the moonlight. It was a peaceful, lovely sight. Ash, a little elf with eyes as wide and curious as the moonlit sky, sat on his window seat. His hair was the color of wet moss. A soft wind blew it. It sounded like a sleepy song. He watched the moon climb higher and higher in the dark, soft sky. It looked like a bright, shiny pearl. Tonight felt special. Tonight felt like a good night to ask a very, very important question.

Ash lived in a little home that was as snug and warm as a bird's nest. It was nestled among the tall, whispering pine trees of the Northwind Heights. His room was a soft, safe place, filled with the gentle glow of moonlight peeking through the leafy branches outside. Beside him sat Corvus, a crow whose feathers were as dark and shiny as a polished stone. Corvus was, well, a little bit bossy. He always seemed to know more than anyone else. His caws often sounded like firm little messages.

"Are you ready now, Ash?" Corvus murmured, fluffing his sleek, dark feathers. "The moon, you know, waits for no elf. But for your information, I think we should have gone by the little stream. It would have been much easier and you wouldn't have wandered."

Ash smiled, a gentle, moonlit smile. "I am ready, Corvus. I have a very important question for the old pine tree."

Corvus tilted his head, his bright eyes shining in the moonlight. "A question? For the pine tree? Well, I'm sure I can answer it. What is it? Tell me, and I'll give you my very best idea."

Ash smiled wider. His eyes sparkled like tiny stars. "It’s a question for the pine tree, Corvus. It feels… important. A special kind of important."

Corvus hopped a little closer. His feet made a soft tap-tap on the wooden seat. "Well, the pine tree might be old and wise in its own way, but it certainly doesn’t have my smarts, or my sharp eyes. Still," he declared, puffing out his chest, "if you must go for this little moonlight walk, I will come with you. For safety, of course. And to give you my helpful advice, which you will surely need."

And so, with Corvus fluttering a little way ahead, or sometimes landing right on his shoulder to offer more "helpful" thoughts, Ash set out. The pine trees sparkled with tiny, soft lights. These were not lamps, but sleepy fireflies blinking their soft hellos as they floated by. The air was cool and smelled so wonderfully of pine needles and damp, sweet earth. It was a calming, peaceful smell that wrapped around them like a soft blanket. Each tiny pine needle seemed to catch the moonlight, making the whole forest gleam like a lovely dream.

Corvus was very busy indeed. "Left here, Ash! No, wait. Definitely right. Or was it left after the third rustling leaf? Honestly, for an elf, you are a little slow to follow my good directions."

Ash chuckled, a soft, sweet sound like tiny bells. "The pine tree isn't far, Corvus. And look," he whispered, pointing to a patch of moss that glowed with a soft, silver light. "It's like the moon sprinkled fairy dust on the ground. Isn't it pretty?"

They ambled along, the gentle whispering of the pine needles sounding like a soft, leafy music box. Suddenly, a warm, sweet smell drifted through the air. It smelled of toasted nuts and something wonderfully baked, like a warm hug in a smell. They rounded some old, mossy ferns and found a small, glowing hollow. There, a little goblin baker, round and rosy-cheeked with flour on his nose, was pulling a tray of golden cookies from a tiny oven in a mossy mound. His name was Grumble.

"Well, hello there, little elf!" Grumble rumbled, his voice like a warm hug. "And hello to you, my feathered friend." He winked at Corvus. "Come for a taste of my special moon-kissed pine-nut cookies? They're just out of the oven."

Ash’s nose twitched. The cookies smelled so good, warm and sweet and inviting. Grumble offered Ash a warm cookie. It was still soft in the middle. Ash took a small, careful bite. It was wonderful! Toasted pine nuts, a hint of sweet honey, and the gentle warmth of the moon seemed to be baked right into the cookie. It was scrumptious—that means really, really yummy!

"Oh, thank you, Mr. Grumble," Ash said, his voice a little muffled with cookie. "They are truly wonderful. The best I have ever tasted."

Grumble beamed, his rosy cheeks glowing even brighter. "Just happy to share a little sweetness with travellers," he rumbled warmly. "Making happy tummies is the best kind of magic, I always say. It fills the whole world with smiles."

Corvus, always ready to investigate a good smell, swooped down and pecked at a dropped crumb. "Hmm. Not bad," he cawed, his voice sounding a little less bossy. "A bit too sweet, perhaps. But still, quite good."

Ash, holding his half-eaten cookie, smiled at the jolly goblin baker. He felt a quiet joy bloom inside him, warm and soft like a new flower. He had been so focused on his important question that he’d almost forgotten to enjoy the journey, the lovely sights and smells, and the kind company. The goblin’s gentle words about sharing happiness made him feel warm all over.

As they left Grumble’s cozy hollow, the path seemed to lead them deeper into the woods, and Ash’s earlier sure feeling began to wobble, just a little. He stopped, a tiny, thoughtful line appearing between his eyebrows. He looked around at the shimmering trees, the soft, dappled light, and Corvus, who was now smoothing his feathers as if he had planned the whole cookie surprise himself.

"Corvus," Ash whispered, his voice losing some of its earlier lightness. "I… I think I’ve forgotten something very important."

Corvus paused his preening, one wing held mid-air. "Forgotten what? Your manners? I told you to say thank you again. Or perhaps you forgot where you put your other sock? Always keep track of your socks, Ash. Very important for keeping your feet warm and your mind clear."

Ash shook his head, a little fluttery worry starting to bloom gently in his chest, like a little cloud in a sunny sky. "No, not my socks, Corvus. My question. For the pine tree. I… I don't remember what it was anymore. It’s gone."

The woods, which had seemed so friendly and full of wonder moments ago, now felt a little quiet, a little hushed. The moon was still bright and beautiful, but Ash felt a small, lonely feeling begin to settle over him. He sat down carefully on a smooth, moss-covered stone, which felt cool and soft beneath him. The important question, the one that had felt so big and clear and bright just moments ago, was now like a wisp of smoke, vanished into the night air.

Corvus hopped off his shoulder and landed softly on the mossy ground beside him. For once, he wasn’t cawing orders or giving bossy advice. He nudged Ash’s elbow gently with his beak, a surprisingly tender touch. "Don't fret so, Ash," Corvus murmured, his voice softer than usual, almost a whisper. "Sometimes the biggest questions are the ones that like to hide. They don't run away, you see, they just… rest for a little while." He looked up at the moon, then back at Ash with his smart, dark eyes. "Perhaps the journey itself, and the delicious cookie, was part of the answer, yes? A little moment of joy before the big thought."

Ash looked at Corvus, surprised by his gentle tone. The crow was right, in his own bossy, Crow-like way. The cookie had been sweet, the woods had shimmered with magic, and Grumble’s laugh had been warm and welcoming. He thought about the goblin’s words: "Making happy tummies is the best kind of magic."

Suddenly, a little spark flickered in Ash’s mind, a tiny glow getting brighter and brighter. He remembered sitting on his windowsill, watching the moon, and feeling a question bloom inside him, warm and true. It wasn't a complicated question, not one about faraway stars or hidden treasures. It was simpler, and much more important. It was about… belonging. About feeling safe and loved and just right.

Ash stood up, a gentle, quiet resolve settling over him, calming his worries. "Thank you, Corvus," he whispered, his voice steady and clear. "I remember now. The question is back." He smiled at the old pine tree, its branches reaching like welcoming, leafy arms towards the sky, as if calling him closer. He walked towards it, the moonlight tracing his path on the forest floor. He stood at its ancient, gnarled base, feeling its strong, steady presence.

"Old Pine Tree," Ash said softly, his voice clear and calm in the quiet night. "My important question is this: Am I home?"

The old pine tree seemed to sigh, a soft, rustling whisper of its needles that sounded like a gentle, loving answer. A single, perfect pinecone, smooth and round, dropped softly at Ash’s feet, a silent reply. The moonlight bathed him in its warm, comforting glow, and he felt a deep, quiet answer settle within him, like a warm stone in his heart. Yes, he was home.

He picked up the pinecone, a small, special reminder of the Northwind Heights, a memory of this peaceful adventure. He broke off a tiny piece of his remaining cookie and offered it to Corvus. Corvus, surprisingly, took it without a single squawk of complaint, his dark eyes soft.

"Well," Corvus murmured, munching contentedly on the sweet treat. "That was a rather well-asked question, Ash. And a well-deserved cookie, indeed. A most happy ending to our little outing."

The journey back felt shorter, bathed in the same gentle, reassuring moonlight. The woods whispered softly, no longer mysterious, but familiar and welcoming, like old friends. Soon, they saw the warm, inviting glow of Ash’s home. He stepped inside, feeling safe and sound, the precious pinecone clutched gently in his hand.

Ash snuggled into his cozy bed, the moonlight painting soft, sleepy shapes on his quilt. Corvus settled on his perch, tucking his head under his wing, ready for his own rest. Ash closed his eyes, the gentle rhythm of the night lulling him towards slumber. The important question had been asked, and the answer was a warm, quiet peace that settled over him like a soft, downy blanket. Soon, he drifted off to sleep, dreaming of sweet pine nuts and shimmering moonbeams, safe and sound in his beloved, peaceful home.
characters: Ash the young elf, a crow
